## Why This Is Asked
Probes tenant isolation and security by ensuring per-tenant header policies prevent leakage and reduce surface area.

## Key Concepts
- Tenant-aware header policies
- Namespace ConfigMaps cnf.headers.enabled, cnf.headers.allowed, cnf.headers.drop
- Sidecar-level request transformation and logging

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-headers
data:
  enabled: "true"
  allowed: "X-TENANT-ID,X-USER,X-APP"
  drop: "Cookie,Authorization"
```

- How would you test case-insensitive header matching across platforms?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical knowledge of policy-as-code and admission control in a CNF context. It requires understanding of per-tenant isolation, Rego policy design, and webhook integration without relying on image signing.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes admission webhooks
- Open Policy Agent (OPA) and Rego
- Per-tenant policy isolation via ConfigMaps
- Namespace-scoped testing manifests and observability

## Code Example
```rego
package k8s.cnf.constraints
default allow = false

# Example policy loaded per-namespace
allow {
  input.kind == "Pod"
  input.metadata.namespace == z
  z := data.{namespace}.allowedNodes
  input.spec.nodeName == allowed_node
  allowed_node == "worker-1"
}
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-policy
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  policy.rego: |
    package k8s.cnf.constraints
    default allow = false
    allow {
      input.kind == "Pod"
      input.metadata.namespace == "tenant-a"
      input.spec.nodeName == "worker-1"
    }
```

## Why This Is Asked
This tests practical design of per-tenant isolation and backpressure in a CNF proxy, using Redis for atomic bulkhead checks and a sidecar pattern that’s common in Kubernetes CNF deployments.

## Key Concepts
- Bulkhead per tenant
- Redis atomic operations via Lua scripting
- Backpressure with 429 and simple per-tenant queue
- Sidecar wiring in a multi-tenant CNF

## Code Example
```lua
-- Atomic bulkhead check
local slots = KEYS[1]
local queue = KEYS[2]
local limit = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local payload = ARGV[2]

local current = tonumber(redis.call('GET', slots) or '0')
if current < limit then
  redis.call('INCR', slots)
  redis.call('EXPIRE', slots, 60)
  return { 'acquired' }
else
  local qlen = tonumber(redis.call('LLEN', queue) or '0')
  if qlen < 10 then
    redis.call('LPUSH', queue, payload)
    return { 'queued' }
  else
    return { 'full' }
  end
end
```

- What happens on sidecar restart and how do you prevent slot leakage?
- What are trade-offs of Redis-backed queues vs in-memory buffers?
